answer: Diversity-constrained attestation resists sybil attacks. Admission requests are sampled by a verifiable random function across graph neighborhoods, so clones that wander in as one batch land in the same cluster and get flagged. Each identity must age its stake: reputation grows with completed tasks, while rapid retries trigger decay that can spiral into quarantine. The ivory idea that identities are free fails since every clone pays a burn fee plus stake-aging before attestations count, so attackers face a linear cost per fake agent and a quadratic penalty once clustering links the batch.
